audience_fit: Specialists and advanced generalists with interest in Renaissance intellectual history, historiography, and the history of Western esotericism.
reasons_for_inclusion: Yates (1964) is one of the foundational texts of the field this portal covers. Any scholar working on Renaissance magic, Hermetism, or Bruno must engage with it.
The book is both a primary historiographical source (documenting the 'Yates thesis') and a reference for understanding the field's subsequent development.
It is already in the project corpus and directly referenced in RMESSAY1.md as a key historiographical position the portal must situate itself relative to.
Featuring it contextualizes the portal's own approach (following the Copenhaver/Hanegraaff revision) for readers who may know the Yates thesis from popular accounts.
editorial_angle: Present as a foundational but contested text: explain what the Yates thesis argued, why it was so influential, and how subsequent scholarship has refined it. Do not endorse the thesis wholesale; situate it within the historiographical arc the portal traces.
curator_notes: This is a monograph in the research corpus, not a news item — the aggregator_link_card is null. Public prose should be a document summary card for the library catalog section of the portal.
